newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Femcotec 25 pct surge baffles dealers.
newsitem.headline: Femcotec 25 pct surge baffles dealers.

text.p: Shares in South African electric motor and components firm, Femco Technologies Ltd (Femcotec), surged on Tuesday, increasing their value by a quarter but the rise amid active trade left dealers baffled.
"It's a mixed bag of guys buying and selling here," said one dealer whose firm had executed a buy order for a client.

By lunchtime Femcotec had added 10 cents, or 25 percent, to 50 cents, its highest level since October 14 last year, making it the morning's biggest gainer on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE). Volumes were heavy at 241,200 shares.
One dealer said the sudden interest could be on the back of rumours that the firm may seek to delist.
Femcotec directors could not be reached for comment.
"There was talk last year that it might delist...If they were going to do that and there was an offer to minorities, it would be a good reason for the share price to go up," the dealer said.

Femcotec, which is the process of a restructure, bounced back into the black in the eight months ended December 31 making attributable profit of 250,000 rand compared with a 21.86 million rand loss in the year ended April 30, 1995.
The JSE said last November that the audit opinon Femcotec's annual financial statements had been qualified. No reasons were given at the time.
